groups.name: Work-domain pruning, compaction, and bounded paging
mechanisms: domain specialization from admitted screening facts

current_owners.responsibility: Represent and specialize active execution domains without duplicating scientific screening policy.
Own physical screening and error criteria supplied to the compiler as admitted facts.

groups.retained_boundary: The compiler may compact an admitted domain but must not invent or relax the scientific screening threshold.

groups.name: Exact specialization and bounded workspace sizing
mechanisms: compile-time removal of unused recurrence state

current_owners.responsibility: Own specialization identities and exact resolved program shapes.
Bind legal target schedules and bounded workspace shapes.

groups.retained_boundary: Specialization follows semantic and target facts; method names and benchmark fingerprints are not dispatch keys.

groups.name: Multi-output common-work fusion and derivative recovery

current_owners.responsibility: Own reusable multi-root scientific DAG sharing and generated derivative products.
Choose fusion, fission, and rematerialization under resource evidence.

groups.retained_boundary: Cross-output sharing is legal only when it preserves declared numerical and derivative semantics.

groups.name: Persistent, resident, cooperative, and signature-aware schedules

current_owners.responsibility: Represent reusable schedule families and measured target-aware selection.
Bind queues, streams, resident state, and backend resources without owning scientific equations.

groups.retained_boundary: Queue and residency mechanics remain runtime/schedule concerns rather than duplicate scientific implementations.

groups.name: Precision placement as a schedule dimension

current_owners.responsibility: Represent explicit precision schedules and typed cast boundaries.
Own numerical promotion, strict refinement, and retained negative evidence.

groups.retained_boundary: Lower precision is an execution schedule and never changes the requested scientific target or its final strict gates.

groups.name: Data residency, lifetime, layout propagation, and zero-copy ownership

current_owners.responsibility: Own alias/lifetime/layout analysis and legal materialization elimination.
Own actual allocations, placements, transfers, and observed resource high-water marks.

groups.retained_boundary: Logical lifetime analysis does not replace backend allocation ownership or silently extend borrowed lifetimes.

groups.name: DFT tile, batch, fusion, and resource-aware schedule search

current_owners.responsibility: Own DFT schedule legality, search, and complete-endpoint promotion.
Provide reusable schedule and profitability primitives without a DFT-only optimizer.

groups.retained_boundary: DFT scientific legality stays with the DFT owner while generic scheduling mechanisms remain reusable.

groups.name: Runtime/controller optimizations outside scalar compiler passes

current_owners.responsibility: Own lifecycle, replay, capture, and bounded structured execution.
Own explicit provider/algorithm choices when they change numerical algorithms or approximations.

groups.retained_boundary: Generic scalar optimization must not absorb convergence policy, solver history, or approximation-changing provider selection.

negative_evidence.reason: A legal bounded split-Gram candidate did not establish an endpoint win.
negative_evidence.promotion_rule: Keep the candidate disabled unless a complete matched endpoint demonstrates a reproducible benefit.

negative_evidence.reason: The bounded two-iteration CUDA RKS control path had no reproducible endpoint benefit.
negative_evidence.promotion_rule: Do not promote replay/control-flow work from launch-count or microbenchmark evidence alone.

negative_evidence.reason: Lower-precision local work can lose after conversion, strict refinement, and duplicate final-state work are counted.
negative_evidence.promotion_rule: Price preparation, conversion, refinement, retry, and finalization before promoting a precision schedule.
